answer: Sequential proof-of-work identity chain. Each new agent identity must extend a shared hash chain, publishing a partial preimage that acts as a costly signal of elapsed compute and unique chain position. Registration encodes the result in a per-agent cipher tied to that slot, so copies fail verification. A public mesa ledger records chain order, preventing parallel forks. Attacker cost: sustained sequential compute per identity, non-parallelizable, so N identities cost N times the work and cannot be shortcut by capital.
